ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A 50 Hz synchronous generator is initially connected to a long lossless transmission line which is open circuited at the receiving end. With the field voltage held constant, the generator is disconnected from the transmission line. Which of the following may be said about the steady-state terminal voltage and field current of the generator?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The magnitude of terminal voltage decreases, and the field current does not change.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The schematic diagram shows a synchronous generator connected to a long transmission line labeled “Long Transmission line”; the right end of the line is the receiving end, and the whole is consistent with the textual description of the question. Reasoning: The question clearly says that when the generator is disconnected from the transmission line, the excitation voltage is kept constant. According to the specified method, regard the rotor excitation winding as an independent DC circuit. In steady state, the excitation current satisfies If = Vf / Rf. Since the excitation voltage Vf is unchanged and the excitation winding resistance Rf is also unchanged, the steady-state excitation current If will not change because the generator is disconnected from the long open-circuit transmission line.

method.method_draft: Read that the generator is initially feeding a long lossless line open at the receiving end, then is disconnected, with field voltage held constant. Recognize that the disconnection removes the line charging current and changes the stator-side operating point/terminal voltage. However, the rotor excitation source is specified to remain at the same field voltage, so the excitation current in steady state is not changed by the stator-side disconnection. Therefore the field current remains unchanged.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses synchronous-machine excitation/armature-reaction reasoning: distinguishes changes in terminal voltage caused by removing the capacitive line from changes in the rotor excitation current. This is weakly distinct from the direct field-circuit method because both rely on constant excitation, but it routes through machine operating behavior.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the line as a long transmission line with an open receiving end, implying the generator initially sees a capacitive/no-load line condition rather than a real load.
planner_metadata.text_role: Provides the initial condition of an open-circuited long line, the operation of disconnection, and the fixed field-voltage constraint.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: A long open-circuited lossless line can supply/absorb reactive effects and alter terminal voltage via charging current/Ferranti effect. Disconnecting it changes stator current and armature reaction, hence terminal voltage, but it does not by itself alter the separately supplied rotor field current when field voltage is regulated constant.
